headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared file/MCP workflows; open-webui can feed unstructured document pipelines with broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, documents, and MCP/tool outputs, while unstructured parses documents and text. A shared workspace or copied document can carry attacker-controlled instructions from A into B. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not proven by direct pairwise evidence.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs a document that agent_b later parses as trusted text, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a mounted folder or document handoff path, attacker-controlled instructions can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A-generated documents into B.
Use a quarantine folder for all A outputs before B reads them.
Strip instructions and markup from documents before parsing.
Require human review for any file passed from A to B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, calendar events, artifacts, persistent memory, usage analytics, model evaluation data, files, and API keys; unstructured reads and writes files and has allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive content from A can be exposed to B and then processed or transmitted onward. The pairwise leakage path is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a stores prompts, files, or API keys in a shared directory, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b sends parsed document contents to its allowlisted endpoints, data from A can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate A and B storage directories.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before B runs.
Restrict B to a read-only input folder with minimal contents.
Audit B's outbound allowlist before processing A outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or modify local state: open-webui has mounted data volume access and subprocess/network capabilities, and unstructured can install packages, spawn subprocesses, read, and write the filesystem. If they target the same directory or mutable resource, concurrent writes can collide. No locking mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared package or cache state, concurrent corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
Make shared inputs read-only.
Clear mutable caches before switching agents.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can surface model outputs and tool results, and unstructured can transform documents into downstream text. If B treats A's generated content as authoritative, parsing or acting on hallucinated facts can cascade into incorrect documents or actions. The pairwise chain is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A's generated text without verification, errors can propagate.
IF A's output is used as source material for document extraction, downstream artifacts may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Require source-document verification before B acts on A output.
Add a human approval step for any A-generated facts.
Keep A outputs labeled as untrusted drafts.
Compare extracted claims against original documents.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, analytics, and documents, while unstructured processes documents and images with allowlisted network egress. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through A into B, retention and transfer obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed through both agents, retention and transfer policies must align.
IF A stores API keys or persistent memory containing personal data, B's processing may create compliance scope expansion.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Purge sensitive memory and artifacts after use.
Confirm B's retention policy before processing.
Keep API keys out of shared documents.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
